motif.name: Betrayal
motif.description: Passages of the piano score that match one melody, in levels by how close they are to it. Level 1 is the closest. A run of repeated notes counts as one note. Passages that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other, are joined into one; the level is that of the closest.

source.author: J. K. Holman
source.title: Wagner's Ring: A Listener's Companion & Concordance
source.publication: Portland, Oregon: Amadeus Press, 1996; paperback 2003, ISBN 978-1-57467-070-7

levels.label: Original
levels.name: The melody as given
levels.description: The melody as you gave it. It is not a passage of the score.

levels.name: Closest to the original
levels.description: The best partial matches of the whole phrase. The pitches and the rhythm are the same, in any octave.

levels.name: Same core pitches
levels.description: Notes 1 to 9 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, but the rhythm differs. In a sung passage the score may have one short extra note between two of them: it is skipped.

levels.name: One note different
levels.description: Notes 1 to 9 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, except one note. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Other keys
levels.description: Notes 1 to 9 of the phrase have the same intervals, moved to another key, in any octave. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Opening, other keys
levels.description: Only the first notes, 1 to 8 of the phrase, have the same intervals, moved to another key. The rhythm may differ. Short cells also match by chance, so some of these passages are coincidences.

occurrences.label: The original
occurrences.note: The melody as you gave it, engraved from your notes. It has no pickup, the bars are in 4/4, and the score has a treble clef and no key signature. It is not a passage of the score.

occurrences.label: Same pitches, one note different
occurrences.note: Your notes 1 to 9 (of 9) have the same pitches here, except one. Your note 7 is F; the score has G there. The rhythm differs. In eighth notes, the score plays them as 9 9 3 3 3 3 2 1 1; yours are 10 2 3 1 10 2 3 1 2.

libretto.text: mein Vöglein, der bin ja ich!
libretto.translation: my little bird, that one is indeed me!

libretto.text: Noch heute gab ich vergebens mir Müh’,
libretto.translation: Even today I took pains in vain,

libretto.text: das Fürchten von Fafner zu lernen:
